Below is a brief summary of what’s happening and two small patches to correct it in `src/resources/filters/quarto-pre/callout.lua`.

1.  Bug scenario  
    – You have a callout caption like  
       “Text in **strong**, and some `code`” or “Text, separated with comma”  
    – In HTML things look fine, but in the LaTeX/PDF path  
      • all your Markdown formatting is dropped (no bold, no verbatim)  
      • commas or percent signs in the caption are fed directly into the tcolorbox options and get parsed as pgfkeys, so you get errors like  
        `I do not know the key '/tcb/separated with comma'`  
    – Root cause: the caption AST is being flattened with `pandoc.utils.stringify()` (so you lose Markdown) and then interpolated raw into the `title=` option of tcolorbox (so commas/percent aren’t escaped or wrapped in braces).

2.  Fix  
    a) Render the caption as actual LaTeX instead of plain text  
    b) Wrap the resulting LaTeX caption string in `{…}` when passing to tcolorbox

With these two changes:

- your Markdown-style strong (`**…**`) and inline code will actually be typeset in LaTeX,  
- and commas, percent signs, braces, etc. in the caption won’t be mis-parsed as tcolorbox options.
